title: Control Plane Loop Registry
assertions: closed loops must bind business claims to code, tests, generated docs, and semantic hashes
business claim meaning changes must co-change at least one bound code or test file in pull requests
bound code or test file changes must co-change the claim registry manifest or generated claim evidence
harness loops must promote failures into closed-loop candidates by running tools/harnesspromotion and publishing strict candidate evidence
claim evidence must expose code, test, manifest, generated doc, verifier surface, and evidence chain ids so agents can infer required co-change and reasoning scope without reading prose
all loops with evidence expiry must declare a scheduled refresh workflow whose cadence is no slower than expiry and publishes strict evidence
loop registry and evidence graph evidence must carry generated_at and expires_at so tools can reject stale evidence
evidence graph evidence must expose full reasoning chains, not only chain ids
closed-loop candidate evidence artifacts must carry generated_at and expires_at so stale promotion, intake, and decision evidence can be rejected
refresh workflows must declare the loop ids they refresh so workflow edits cannot drift away from the loop registry manifest
AI agents do not need to read the prose doc when the verifier can enforce the bound surface

harness_workflow_exclusions.reason: generated endpoint smoke matrix is a contract and generator gate, not a live exploratory harness that discovers runtime failures
harness promotion is the closed-loop candidate promotion sidecar consumed by harness loops, not a source harness

claim_bindings.statement: Deleting an agent must not delete or hide prior task thread replies, result messages, progress lines, or captured agent snapshot.
AI thread history must preserve user follow-up messages and restore them after persistence reloads.
Multiple agents backed by the same provider must remain distinct assignments and threads across assignment, message posting, listing, and SSE filters.

AI thread history v3 must expose a stable conversation_id for agent comment card grouping, preserve that conversation_id for follow-up replies, expose parent_thread_id for follow-up runs, and allocate a different conversation_id for same-agent reassignment.

Redacted live workflow summaries must declare generated_at and expires_at, and harness promotion must reject expired or malformed summary freshness metadata before writing closed-loop candidate evidence.

The AI Agent load and stress harness must run on a schedule, publish redacted live summary evidence, and promote failed runs into closed-loop candidate artifacts without exposing raw endpoint, token, or response data.
Harness refresh workflows must run both harnesspromotion and closed-loop candidate artifact upload under if: always(), so a failing smoke or load run still produces closed-loop candidate evidence.

Closed-loop candidate artifacts must include an adoption_plan that maps every required_next_artifact to an executable command, and intake/decision verifiers must reject candidates whose adoption plan is missing or incomplete.

Closed-loop candidate artifacts must include a promotion_edge matching the source harness loop, closed-loop target, and promotes_failure_to relation, and intake/decision evidence must expose that edge so agents can follow the failure-to-closed-loop path without reading narrative docs.
Closed-loop verifier tools must accept the common -verify intent as an alias for their generated-doc verification mode so agents do not need tool-specific flag memory.

Every redacted evidence artifact declared by an expiring loop must be produced by a scheduled refresh workflow that declares the loop id, fits the loop expiry window, and uploads that exact artifact with strict if-no-files-found behavior.

When task context is marketing, analysis, planning, or otherwise intent-oriented rather than an explicit instruction, the assignment prompt must emit intent_gate_required=true and require the agent to ask for intent in the existing thread before producing deliverables; provider token, quota, cloud-credit exhaustion, or local approval-dialog wording must render as a user-facing thread result without changing API shape, and assigning another agent after the limit must create a separate conversation without hiding the prior thread history.

Loop registry evidence must expose each business claim's executable surface across code, tests, manifests, generated docs, verifier names, target verifier commands, and evidence graph chain ids, and each claim must bind at least one code or test path so agents can infer co-change, QA, and reasoning scope without reading narrative docs.

Loop registry CI must emit GitHub Actions annotations for claim verifier commands so reviewers and agents can see the target QA commands directly in the check output without opening generated artifacts or narrative docs.

When a business claim is added, its meaning changes, generated-doc binding changes, or a claim is removed in a pull request, the impact verifier must require at least one bound code or test path to change; manifest-only or generated-doc-only edits are not sufficient proof that runtime meaning was updated.

When a business claim meaning changes in a pull request, the impact verifier must also require the evidence graph reasoning manifest to change so Observation, Hypothesis, Decision, and Next Loop stay aligned with the changed claim.
The local pre-commit hook must run loop-registry generated-doc and impact verification with evidence output, so claim-code-test-doc drift is blocked before PR creation.
Every claim-bound code, test, fixture, manifest, and generated reader path must be covered by the loop-registry workflow trigger paths so PR impact verification runs when any bound surface changes.
Every loop-registry business claim must be referenced by at least one evidence-graph chain, and every chain claim reference must point to an existing loop-registry claim.
Every non-artifact file or workflow referenced by the evidence graph must be covered by the evidence-graph workflow trigger paths so graph verification runs when referenced surfaces move or change.

Evidence graph evidence must publish each chain's observation, hypothesis, changes, verifiers, evidence refs, decision, and next loop so agents can infer why a loop exists without opening narrative docs.

Loop registry and evidence graph evidence artifacts must publish generated_at and expires_at, and the evidence graph workflow must run on a schedule so stale reasoning graphs are refreshed without human reminders.

Harness promotion, closed-loop candidate intake, and closed-loop candidate decision evidence artifacts must publish generated_at and expires_at so stale candidate-loop evidence cannot be reused as fresh QA output.
Closed-loop candidate intake verification must consume a candidate artifact before producing intake evidence, so harness failures cannot become passive manifest-only reports.

Every loop with evidence expiry, regardless of expiry duration, must declare a scheduled refresh workflow whose cadence is no slower than the expiry and whose workflow publishes strict redacted evidence.

Every refresh workflow named by the loop registry must declare RIIDO_LOOP_IDS with the loop ids it refreshes, so workflow-only edits still expose their semantic loop ownership to verifiers and agents.
Loop registry evidence must expose per-loop refresh_plans that bind each expiring loop to its refresh workflow, cadence, expiry, redacted evidence artifacts, and manual QA refresh command.

Loop registry evidence must expose the executable evidence_graph edge list, not only edge counts, and every harness promotes_to target must have a matching promotes_failure_to graph edge so agents can infer loop-to-claim and harness-to-candidate paths from the artifact without opening narrative docs.
Every smoke, load, or harness workflow must either be registered as a harness loop that promotes failures into closed-loop candidates or be explicitly excluded with a machine-readable reason.

Closed-loop candidate decision verification must consume a candidate artifact, and decision records must match that artifact exactly: every candidate needs one decision, and every decision must point to a current candidate.

Closed-loop candidate decisions must choose a next_artifact that is explicitly required by the consumed candidate artifact, so harness failures cannot be routed to arbitrary or non-executable follow-up work.
Closed-loop candidate decision evidence must expose the executable next_command selected from the consumed candidate adoption_plan for the chosen next_artifact.

loop.observation: AI agents can skip or misunderstand narrative docs, while previously fixed AI thread regressions can reappear when related files are edited independently.
loop.hypothesis: A loop registry can make the intended QA loop executable by binding business claims to code files, tests, generated docs, semantic hashes, evidence expiry, and harness promotion paths.
loop.execute: Generate this reader from the loop registry, verify claim-code-test-doc bindings, require each expiring loop to name a scheduled refresh workflow whose cadence is no slower than expiry and publishes strict evidence, require harness workflows to run tools/harnesspromotion and upload strict candidate evidence, compute claim semantic hashes, enforce PR impact co-change for claim meaning changes and bound file changes, and publish redacted evidence in CI.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails on missing loop fields, missing tests, missing bound files, stale generated docs, missing scheduled refresh workflow coverage, refresh cadence slower than evidence expiry, missing strict refresh evidence, harness workflows without candidate promotion, unknown graph nodes, semantic hash drift, claim meaning changes without bound code/test changes, or bound code/test changes without claim evidence changes.
loop.retrospective: This moves the human out of the inner loop: a future AI can change code without reading this prose, but cannot merge drift without updating the executable claim binding and evidence.
